deviations_assessment.deviation: genesis-concurrency: seed-head INSERT ON CONFLICT (tenant_id) DO NOTHING (seq=0/GENESIS_PREV_HASH) then always FOR UPDATE→UPDATE-advance, replacing the ADR §4.2 retry-on-unique-on-event-INSERT.
deviations_assessment.reasoning: ADR §4.2 explicitly sanctioned this as the named alternative ('coder chooses; invariant = N dense seq'). The chosen path is strictly safer: it serializes from the very first append via a single FOR UPDATE on a guaranteed-present head row, so there is no dup-PK race on the event-INSERT (which the ADR's retry-on-unique would have had to recover from). Verified live: N=8 (suite) and N=24 (reviewer stress) → dense distinct 1..N, zero failures. The seed row at seq=0 never trips trigger 007 (INSERT, not UPDATE) and is invisible as an audit row (audit_event chain starts at seq=1). InMemory path uses GENESIS_SEQ=1 directly with prev=GENESIS_PREV_HASH — byte-identical first-row hash to the Postgres path (confirmed by live recompute equality).

deviations_assessment.deviation: verb='transition' (ADR §4.7 prose) vs the CLOSED ActorEventVerb set {request,prepare,submit,approve,release} (migration 018 / actor-event.ts).
deviations_assessment.verdict: TYPE-SOUND / accept (ADR prose is a nit, not the code)
deviations_assessment.reasoning: The code is correct and type-sound: LifecycleGuardInput.verb is typed as ActorEventVerb (the closed set), and GuardContext.verb: ActorEventVerb (grant-resolver.ts:377). There is NO free-string 'transition' verb anywhere in the actor_event vocabulary — the literal 'transition' that exists in the codebase is Grant.operation (the gated OP-CLASS, op==='approve'||op==='transition'), a DIFFERENT vocabulary from the verb WRITTEN to actor_event. lifecycle-guard.ts:30 documents this correctly ('a transition maps onto one of the closed verbs e.g. submit/release'). The ADR §4.7 wording verb='transition'|'approve' is loose and contradicts its own foundation (T-0019/018); it should read 'verb ∈ ActorEventVerb'. No code change needed; the ADR prose drift is recorded as nit R-3 (architect doc-fix). Migration 018 CHECK stays ('request','prepare','submit','approve','release') and FF-8 confirms employee schema unchanged.

dual_chain_writers_assessment: CONFLICT-RISK (not a benign forward) — record for orchestrator, blocks the T-0030 forward-obligation, does NOT block T-0068 merge by itself. After dev@91f991e merged T-0030, src/http/grants.ts now carries a LOCAL chain writer appendAuditEventInput() that writes the SAME tables (choros.audit_event / choros.audit_head, vocab_version=1) as T-0068's canonical writer, but with an INCOMPATIBLE preimage: it computes row_hash = SHA-256(prevHash || type || actor || (subject??'') || String(occurred_at)) — a partial, NON-length-prefixed, NON-JCS digest that does NOT cover id, tenant_id, seq, scope, via, proposed_by, confirmed_by, payload, or prev_hash framing. T-0068's canonicalPreimage covers all 14 fields length-prefixed + JCS. Both stamp vocab_version=1, so a verifier (T-0053) recomputing per vocab=1 would FALSE-POSITIVE tamper on every grant-trail row, OR, if grant + lifecycle events interleave in one tenant chain, the two hash rules break chain density verification outright. This is exactly the 'forward false-positive vs conflict' the ADR §3/§4.1 anti-pattern warned against ('развилка стока → два preimage-пути'). T-0030's own commit note ('chain columns computed locally until T-0053') framed it as a placeholder, but the placeholder uses vocab_version=1 (a CLAIM of canonical encoding) rather than an unpinned/0 sentinel, so it is not safely forward-compatible. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP: when T-0030's documented forward-obligation lands (ADR §9: 'writeGrantAuditEvent must call T-0068 appendAuditEvent — single sink'), grants.ts MUST drop appendAuditEventInput() and route through makePgAuditWriter().appendAuditEvent (the AuditEventInput contract is already compatible — §4.1). Until then, NO production tenant may carry BOTH grant-trail and lifecycle audit rows, or the chain is unverifiable. T-0068 itself is correct (canonical, single-writer per FF-11 within its own branch); the conflict is a dev-integration debt owned by the T-0030↔T-0068 reconciliation, to be triaged before either writer goes live end-to-end.

findings.issue: The lifecycle-audit runtime path is dead in production — NOTHING appends a lifecycle audit row from the wired entry point. (a) index.ts:27 calls startLifecycleBridge() with NO deps, so the guard at lifecycle-bridge.ts:151 (deps.pool===undefined || deps.jobStore===undefined) returns a no-op handle UNCONDITIONALLY, even when FLOWABLE_BASE_URL is set — the bridge can never start from main. (b) Even if deps were passed, buildAuditOnDispatched(...) is only `void`-referenced (line 159) and its onDispatched callback is discarded: startBridgePollLoop (the fetch/lock half) has no onDispatched param (ExternalTaskBridgeConfig carries none), and the outbox dispatcher (runOutboxOnce / makeExternalTaskDeliver — the actual onDispatched firing point) is NOT started anywhere in production (only in bridge-smoke-runner.ts, a CI entrypoint, and there makeExternalTaskDeliver is called WITHOUT the audit callback). (c) auditInstanceStarted has no production call-site. Net: FR-3/FR-4/FR-8 ('путь инстанса виден в аудит-логе' at runtime) is not deliverable; the in-code comment 'the outbox dispatcher consumes the same callback' is false — no prod dispatcher consumes it. The unit tests (AC-7/AC-8 in-memory + direct calls) and FF-9 grep pass over a seam that no runtime path exercises. This is the integration-honesty gate (D-056): BUILD asserts wiring it does not deliver.
findings.suggestion: Make the wiring real OR honestly narrow the claim. Minimum to satisfy FR-8 at runtime: (1) index.ts must construct and pass pool + PostgresJobStore (and an outbox store) into startLifecycleBridge; (2) start the OUTBOX dispatcher loop (runOutboxOnce on an interval) with onDispatched=makeAuditOnDispatched(...), since that — not startBridgePollLoop — is where task_completed/task_failed fire; pass the audit callback into makeExternalTaskDeliver(flowableClient, jobStore, auditOnDispatched). (3) Call auditInstanceStarted from the real startInstance call-site (or, if no HTTP route exists yet, state that explicitly in the PR handoff as a named forward-obligation with the route task id, rather than shipping an uncalled wrapper). If the team's position is that live end-to-end is genuinely deferred to a later route task, then the spec/ADR/PR must say the runtime audit path is INERT in this build (seam only) and FR-8's 'loop стартует' claim must be downgraded — do not leave a `void`-ed callback + dep-less startLifecycleBridge() reading as if it works.

findings.issue: `void buildAuditOnDispatched(deps.pool, deps.resolveActor);` with the comment 'Touch the audit onDispatched wiring so the composition is exercised' — this is dead code whose only effect is to satisfy a reader/linter that the symbol is used. It builds a writer + closure and throws them away. Misleading: it reads as wiring but wires nothing (see R-1).
findings.suggestion: Remove the void-touch once R-1 is addressed (the callback will then be passed to a real dispatcher). If kept temporarily, the comment must say it is a NO-OP placeholder, not 'the composition is exercised'.

findings.issue: ADR §4.7 specifies buildLifecycleGuardCtx with verb='transition'|'approve', but 'transition' is NOT a member of the closed ActorEventVerb set (migration 018 / actor-event.ts = {request,prepare,submit,approve,release}). The code (lifecycle-guard.ts) correctly types verb: ActorEventVerb and rejects 'transition' at compile time, so the implementation is right and the ADR prose is wrong. Also §4.8 ADR text describes startBridgePollLoop({..., onDispatched: makeAuditOnDispatched(...)}) but startBridgePollLoop has no onDispatched parameter — the ADR mis-specified the firing point (it is the outbox dispatcher, not the poll loop). This ADR mis-spec is the root of R-1: the coder 'implemented' an impossible signature by void-ing the callback instead of flagging the ADR error.
findings.suggestion: Architect doc-fix: §4.7 → 'verb ∈ ActorEventVerb (a process transition maps to submit/release)'. §4.8 → onDispatched belongs to makeExternalTaskDeliver/runOutboxOnce (outbox dispatcher), not startBridgePollLoop; correct the composition description so the wiring obligation in R-1 is unambiguous.

findings.issue: JCS key ordering uses Array.prototype.sort() (default lexicographic on UTF-16 code units). RFC 8785 §3.2.3 mandates sorting on UTF-16 code units, which the default sort does provide for the BMP; however the comment at lines 166-167 claims 'sorted by UTF-16 code-unit' which is correct, but there is no test fixture exercising non-ASCII / supratBMP keys to lock this. Choros lifecycle payloads are ASCII today (actorType/instanceId/processKey/aggregateId/errorMessage), so no live risk — but the vocab=1 golden does not pin the non-ASCII key-ordering behavior, so a future payload with unicode keys could drift the encoding without reddening the golden.
findings.suggestion: Add one FF-3 fixture row with a non-ASCII jsonb key (and/or a key pair that differs only above U+FFFF) to pin the JCS ordering under vocab=1, so any future change to the sort comparator flips the golden. Low priority (no current non-ASCII keys), but it closes the only unpinned corner of the canonical encoding.

role_gap_evidence: SQ11 (security-reviewer candidate): the GUC interpolation in lifecycle-bridge.ts:121 (SET LOCAL choros.tenant_id = '${tenantId.replace(/'/g,"''")}') is the ONE place in the codebase that quote-escapes the tenant id before interpolation; pgOutboxStore.ts:202 / pgJobStore.ts:506 / org.ts:86 / audit-grant-trail.ts:92 interpolate raw tenantId with no escaping. Not a T-0068 regression (T-0068 is strictly safer, and tenantId is a trusted UUID), but the systematic raw-interpolation of a GUC across 4+ DAOs is a class-level pattern a security-reviewer should normalize to set_config($1) / parameterized form. Evidence for ledgers/role-gaps.md, not a T-0068 blocker.
